title: The parity conjecture for independence polynomials of generalized Petersen graphs contradicts itself

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
Pandey conjectured that for n ≥ 2k+1 the independence polynomial of the generalized Petersen graph GP(n,k) has only real roots if and only if k is even. John Erlbacher's Demonstrandum project refuted this first, by exact computation, with GP(7,3), GP(9,2) and the isomorphism GP(7,2) ≅ GP(7,3) (doi:10.5281/zenodo.20673864, result 6). We show that the statement contradicts itself: GP(n,2) ≅ GP(n,(n−1)/2) whenever n ≡ 3 (mod 4), and (n−1)/2 is then odd. We also give hand proofs that each direction fails on its own: the independence polynomial of GP(7,3) has only real roots, and that of GP(9,2) has exactly five real roots out of seven.

The archive contains the paper (PDF, LaTeX sources with the figure as PNG, arXiv tarball) and independent checks of every finite claim in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4. A Lean 4 proof with Mathlib covers the isomorphism lemma for every n, the self-contradiction for every n ≡ 3 (mod 4), the refutation of the conjecture as stated, and the root counts, using only the standard axioms; a second Lean file checks the isomorphisms for n ≤ 199, the three polynomials and the numerical inequalities in the kernel.
